text:
Managed-module laws done (the remaining P6f.34 slice).

ControlCommandJsonLawSuite (10 tests): round-trip over all 12 ControlCommand
cases, never-throws over arbitrary / mutated / nested-mutated records,
unknown-field tolerance, bounds, plus non-vacuity and sensitivity guards. The
sensitivity test strips each of retrySafety, epoch, submissionKey, attemptId and
requestDigest from a valid encoding and asserts the round-trip law notices, which
is what proves the law would catch a codec that omitted them.

JournalReplayLawSuite (4 tests): drives the real FileJournalControlStore rather
than JournalCodec, which is file-private on purpose. Law is exact state equality
between the live snapshot and the reopened one, valid because the commit path and
the replay path compact the event cache identically. Also covers checksum
detection of an altered command body (length-preserving digit rewrite) and
encoding determinism, which the checksum depends on.

Shared corpora extracted to protocol's JsonCorpus (arbitraryJson, mutations,
nestedMutations, withUnknownField) so wire and journal decoders are held to the
same three corpora instead of one suite's copy.

Two gaps found and fixed along the way:
- decodeIntent decoded requestBase64 unbounded. A journal frame defaults to 32MB
  while a canonical request is capped at 4MB, so a record could make the reader
  allocate about six times the permitted size before CanonicalRequest.validated
  refused it. Now goes through AgentDomainJson.decodeBase64Bounded, made public
  so the check-before-allocate arithmetic has one home.
- LaunchSpec had no round-trip law despite carrying three defaulted fields.
  Added, and it surfaced that the submit protocol only expresses exit-only
  contracts; added a law that a declared-outputs or structured contract is
  refused rather than silently downgraded, since a downgrade would let a job
  report success with its outputs never collected.

480 tests pass, up from 464. Formatting clean including build.sbt.
